## 22. LONG-TERM LOANS (Continued)

On November 6, 2017, BA entered into a Mutual Agreement with PT Timur Properti Investindo TPI to obtain loan with maximum credit limit of Rp25.00 billion. Based on TPI's Approval Letter regarding BA's Debt Settlement Plan on February 11, 2020, the maturity date of this loan has been extended until June 2026.

The loan is secured by:

a. One (1) unit of office space located at Bakrie Tower, 35th Floor with land area of 1,422 m².
b. Sinking fund comprised of three (3) months of principal and interest totalling Rp4.1 billion.

On March 12, 2020, BA received notification letter of the Transfer Receivable from TPI to Koperasi Simpan Pinjam Timur Pratama Indonesia ("Kospin TPI") based on Sale and Purchase of Receivable Agreement between TPI and Kospin TPI on February 26, 2020. Effective since the date of notification letter, BA loan from TPI has been transferred to Kospin TPI.

On July 13 2021, BA and Kospin TPI signed a Loan Settlement Agreement, which stated that BA's loan to Kospin TPI was Rp29.40 billion, consisting of a principal loan amounting to Rp18.13 billion and interest amounting to Rp11.27 billion. The term of this agreement is valid for sixty (60) months.

According to the Loan Agreement, BA is considered to be in default if it fails to make payments for two (2) consecutive months, and Kospin TPI has the right to initiate an open auction for the collateral of the loan. For each installment payment delay, BA will be charged a penalty of 10% of the installment amount per month.

In December 2024, BA has fully settled all the obligation related to this loan facility.

As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the outstanding loan balance payable to Kospin TPI amounted to nil and Rp15.70 billion, respectively.

# Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)

As part of efforts to improve sustainable corporate governance, BTN has completed a Diagnostic Review of its Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). This process represents a strategic initiative aligned with the directives of the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (KBUMN) based on KBUMN Letter No. S-4/DKU.MBU/02/2024. As part of efforts to strengthen corporate governance, BTN's ICOFR Diagnostic Review project is implemented through a systematic approach consisting of four main stages:

## Stages of Diagnostic Review for ICOFR at BTN

1.  Mapping BTN's corporate structure and assessing risks of material misstatements due to structural complexity. The results serve as a basis for understanding potential risks in financial reporting.

2.  Identifying significant accounts in BTN's financial statements. Each account is analyzed to assess the risks attached, ensuring all elements affecting internal controls are appropriately mapped.

3.  Conducting diagnostic procedures to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in various areas. This process includes interviews with process owners, document reviews of policies and procedures, and in-depth analysis of control implementation.

4.  Comprehensive improvement recommendations are drafted. An implementation roadmap is also designed as a strategic guide for executing improvements in a phased and measurable manner.

Throughout the process, the diagnostic procedures include in-depth interviews, regulatory documents and supporting materials reviews, and identifying areas of control that require improvement. This approach ensures that each step contributes significantly to strengthening BTN's internal controls to support transparent and accountable corporate governance.

In conducting the Diagnostic Review of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR), BTN identified 13 key areas as primary focuses, covering Entity Level Control, IT General Control, and processes in financial, credit, treasury, and HR functions. This process is designed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls across various operational lines of the Bank.

## Diagnostic Review Procedure for ICOFR at BTN

- Understanding processes and controls through interviews with Process Owners and reviews of policy and procedure documents.
- Workthrough
- Controls identified are confirmed through supporting documents for implementation.
- Confirmation
- Reviewing samples of transaction documents to assess the adequacy of controls within a transaction cycle.
- Document Review
- Identifying control areas that require improvement and obtaining confirmation from Process Owners for approval.
- Identification of Areas for Improvement

# Basel Implementation

Basel is an international regulatory framework designed to strengthen the stability of the banking system by improving risk management. In the Indonesian banking sector, Basel implementation is carried out in accordance with OJK regulations to ensure adequate capital, liquidity, and risk management operations.

This framework supports the sustainability of banking businesses by maintaining customer trust and the stability of the financial sector. To implement risk management, particularly the application of Basel II and Basel III, which applies to all commercial banks, BTN has fulfilled the following requirements:

|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 1  |   |
|  The Bank has implemented market risk measurements using the standardized model in accordance with SE OJK No. 38/SEOJK.03/2016, dated September 15, 2016, concerning the Guidelines for Using the Standard Method in Calculating Minimum Capital Requirements for Commercial Banks by Considering Market Risk. The portfolio included in determining the KPMM market risk consists of interest rate trading book portfolios and currency trading book and banking book portfolios for exchange rate risk. The Bank has prepared SEOJK No. 23/SEOJK.03/2022, dated December 7, 2022, regarding the Calculation of Risk-Weighted Assets for Market Risk for Commercial Banks, which has been applied as of January 1, 2024. The Bank has also conducted trial calculations and reporting to OJK for market risk ATMR positions as of June 2023, September 2023, and December 2023. | ☑  |
|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 2  |   |

## 22. PINJAMAN JANGKA PANJANG (Lanjutan)

Pada tanggal 6 November 2017, BA menandatangani Kesepakatan Bersama dengan TPI untuk memperoleh pinjaman dengan plafon maksimal penarikan sebesar Rp25,00 miliar. Berdasarkan Surat Persetujuan TPI tentang Rencana Penyelesaian Utang BA pada tanggal 11 Februari 2020, pinjaman ini telah diperpanjang jatuh temponya sampai dengan Juni 2026.

Pinjaman tersebut dijamin dengan:

a. Satu (1) ruang kantor di Bakrie Tower, Lantai 35 dengan luas 1.422 m².
b. Sinking fund terdiri dari tiga (3) bulan pokok dan bunga sebesar Rp4,1 miliar.

Pada tanggal 12 Maret 2020, BA telah menerima surat pemberitahuan Pengalihan Piutang dari TPI kepada Koperasi Simpan Pinjam Timur Pratama Indonesia ("Kospin TPI") berdasarkan Perjanjian Jual Beli Piutang antara TPI dan Kospin TPI pada tanggal 26 Februari 2020. Efektif sejak tanggal surat pemberitahuan, pinjaman BA dari TPI telah beralih ke Kospin TPI.

Pada tanggal 13 Juli 2021, BA dan Kospin TPI telah menandatangani Perjanjian Penyelesaian Pinjaman, yang menegaskan bahwa pinjaman BA kepada Kospin TPI sebesar Rp29,40 miliar, yang terdiri dari utang pokok sebesar Rp18,13 miliar dan bunga sebesar Rp11,27 miliar. Jangka waktu perjanjian ini berlaku selama enam puluh (60) bulan.

Berdasarkan Perjanjian Pinjaman, BA dianggap telah wanprestasi jika tidak melakukan pembayaran atas angsuran selama dua (2) bulan berturut-turut dan Kospin TPI berhak untuk memulai pelaksanaan lelang terbuka atas jaminan pinjaman. Atas setiap keterlambatan pembayaran angsuran, BA akan dikenakan denda sebesar 10% dari besarnya angsuran setiap bulan.

Pada bulan Desember 2024, BA telah menyelesaikan seluruh kewajiban atas fasilitas pinjaman ini.

Pada tanggal 31 Desember 2024 dan 2023, saldo pinjaman utang kepada Kospin TPI masing-masing sebesar nihil dan Rp15,70 miliar.

## d. PT Bank KB Bukopin Tbk ("Bukopin")

Pada tanggal 11 Desember 2017, PT Bina Usaha Mandiri Mizusawa ("BUMM"), Entitas Anak, menandatangani perjanjian pinjaman dengan PT Bank KB Bukopin Tbk ("Bukopin") untuk menyediakan fasilitas kredit kepada BUMM yang terdiri dari:

1. Fasilitas Kredit Investasi dengan plafon maksimal sebesar Rp3,0 miliar dengan jangka waktu maksimal enam puluh (60) bulan digunakan untuk mengambil alih (take over) pinjaman dari PT Bank BNI Syariah;

## 22. LONG-TERM LOANS (Continued)

On November 6, 2017, BA entered into a Mutual Agreement with PT Timur Properti Investindo TPI to obtain loan with maximum credit limit of Rp25.00 billion. Based on TPI's Approval Letter regarding BA's Debt Settlement Plan on February 11, 2020, the maturity date of this loan has been extended until June 2026.

The loan is secured by:

a. One (1) unit of office space located at Bakrie Tower, 35th Floor with land area of 1,422 m².
b. Sinking fund comprised of three (3) months of principal and interest totalling Rp4.1 billion.

On March 12, 2020, BA received notification letter of the Transfer Receivable from TPI to Koperasi Simpan Pinjam Timur Pratama Indonesia ("Kospin TPI") based on Sale and Purchase of Receivable Agreement between TPI and Kospin TPI on February 26, 2020. Effective since the date of notification letter, BA loan from TPI has been transferred to Kospin TPI.

On July 13 2021, BA and Kospin TPI signed a Loan Settlement Agreement, which stated that BA's loan to Kospin TPI was Rp29.40 billion, consisting of a principal loan amounting to Rp18.13 billion and interest amounting to Rp11.27 billion. The term of this agreement is valid for sixty (60) months.

According to the Loan Agreement, BA is considered to be in default if it fails to make payments for two (2) consecutive months, and Kospin TPI has the right to initiate an open auction for the collateral of the loan. For each installment payment delay, BA will be charged a penalty of 10% of the installment amount per month.

In December 2024, BA has fully settled all the obligation related to this loan facility.

As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the outstanding loan balance payable to Kospin TPI amounted to nil and Rp15.70 billion, respectively.

1. Investment Credit Facility with maximum amount amounting to Rp3.0 billion with maximum term of sixty (60) months to be used for take over of outstanding loan from PT Bank BNI Syariah;

# Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)

As part of efforts to improve sustainable corporate governance, BTN has completed a Diagnostic Review of its Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). This process represents a strategic initiative aligned with the directives of the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (KBUMN) based on KBUMN Letter No. S-4/DKU.MBU/02/2024. As part of efforts to strengthen corporate governance, BTN's ICOFR Diagnostic Review project is implemented through a systematic approach consisting of four main stages:

## Stages of Diagnostic Review for ICOFR at BTN

1.  Mapping BTN's corporate structure and assessing risks of material misstatements due to structural complexity. The results serve as a basis for understanding potential risks in financial reporting.

2.  Identifying significant accounts in BTN's financial statements. Each account is analyzed to assess the risks attached, ensuring all elements affecting internal controls are appropriately mapped.

3.  Conducting diagnostic procedures to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in various areas. This process includes interviews with process owners, document reviews of policies and procedures, and in-depth analysis of control implementation.

4.  Comprehensive improvement recommendations are drafted. An implementation roadmap is also designed as a strategic guide for executing improvements in a phased and measurable manner.

Throughout the process, the diagnostic procedures include in-depth interviews, regulatory documents and supporting materials reviews, and identifying areas of control that require improvement. This approach ensures that each step contributes significantly to strengthening BTN's internal controls to support transparent and accountable corporate governance.

In conducting the Diagnostic Review of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR), BTN identified 13 key areas as primary focuses, covering Entity Level Control, IT General Control, and processes in financial, credit, treasury, and HR functions. This process is designed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls across various operational lines of the Bank.

## Diagnostic Review Procedure for ICOFR at BTN

- Understanding processes and controls through interviews with Process Owners and reviews of policy and procedure documents.
- Workthrough
- Controls identified are confirmed through supporting documents for implementation.
- Confirmation
- Reviewing samples of transaction documents to assess the adequacy of controls within a transaction cycle.
- Document Review
- Identifying control areas that require improvement and obtaining confirmation from Process Owners for approval.
- Identification of Areas for Improvement

Based on the diagnostic results, BTN then prepares a roadmap to ensure the timely and efficient implementation of recommendations. The roadmap preparation involves intensive discussions with BTN management to align all improvement steps with the Company's operational needs. The primary focuses of the roadmap include:

1. Setting implementation priorities based on the risk level and urgency of each recommendation.
2. Continuous monitoring and evaluation to ensure the implementation proceeds as planned and has a positive impact on internal control management.

Additionally, through the implementation of the ICOFR Diagnostic Review, BTN reaffirms its commitment to the principles of Good Corporate Governance. This effort is designed to strengthen internal controls while enhancing transparency and accountability in financial reporting. These steps not only support efficient operational management but also serve as an essential foundation for ensuring BTN's business sustainability in facing future challenges in the banking industry.

# Basel Implementation

Basel is an international regulatory framework designed to strengthen the stability of the banking system by improving risk management. In the Indonesian banking sector, Basel implementation is carried out in accordance with OJK regulations to ensure adequate capital, liquidity, and risk management operations.

This framework supports the sustainability of banking businesses by maintaining customer trust and the stability of the financial sector. To implement risk management, particularly the application of Basel II and Basel III, which applies to all commercial banks, BTN has fulfilled the following requirements:

|  Requirement | Status  |
| --- | --- |
|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 1  |   |
|  The Bank has implemented market risk measurements using the standardized model in accordance with SE OJK No. 38/SEOJK.03/2016, dated September 15, 2016, concerning the Guidelines for Using the Standard Method in Calculating Minimum Capital Requirements for Commercial Banks by Considering Market Risk. The portfolio included in determining the KPMM market risk consists of interest rate trading book portfolios and currency trading book and banking book portfolios for exchange rate risk. The Bank has prepared SEOJK No. 23/SEOJK.03/2022, dated December 7, 2022, regarding the Calculation of Risk-Weighted Assets for Market Risk for Commercial Banks, which has been applied as of January 1, 2024. The Bank has also conducted trial calculations and reporting to OJK for market risk ATMR positions as of June 2023, September 2023, and December 2023. | ☑  |
|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 2  |   |
|  The Bank submitted the results of the implementation report on Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB) and the IRRBB calculation report to regulators quarterly in accordance with SE OJK No. 12/SEOJK.03/2018, dated August 21, 2018, concerning the Implementation of Risk Management and Measurement of Risk Using the Standard Method for Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB). | ☑  |
|  Implementation of Basel III  |   |
|  In accordance with the regulatory plan to implement Basel III as stipulated in OJK Regulation No. 11/POJK.03/2016, the Bank specifically has maintained a Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) of 20.17%, exceeding the minimum requirement of the Basel III framework, which is 10.5%. | ☑  |

# Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)

As part of efforts to improve sustainable corporate governance, BTN has completed a Diagnostic Review of its Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). This process represents a strategic initiative aligned with the directives of the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (KBUMN) based on KBUMN Letter No. S-4/DKU.MBU/02/2024. As part of efforts to strengthen corporate governance, BTN's ICOFR Diagnostic Review project is implemented through a systematic approach consisting of four main stages:

## Stages of Diagnostic Review for ICOFR at BTN

1.  Mapping BTN's corporate structure and assessing risks of material misstatements due to structural complexity. The results serve as a basis for understanding potential risks in financial reporting.

2.  Identifying significant accounts in BTN's financial statements. Each account is analyzed to assess the risks attached, ensuring all elements affecting internal controls are appropriately mapped.

3.  Conducting diagnostic procedures to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in various areas. This process includes interviews with process owners, document reviews of policies and procedures, and in-depth analysis of control implementation.

## 22. PINJAMAN JANGKA PANJANG (Lanjutan)

Pada tanggal 6 November 2017, BA menandatangani Kesepakatan Bersama dengan TPI untuk memperoleh pinjaman dengan plafon maksimal penarikan sebesar Rp25,00 miliar. Berdasarkan Surat Persetujuan TPI tentang Rencana Penyelesaian Utang BA pada tanggal 11 Februari 2020, pinjaman ini telah diperpanjang jatuh temponya sampai dengan Juni 2026.

Pinjaman tersebut dijamin dengan:

a. Satu (1) ruang kantor di Bakrie Tower, Lantai 35 dengan luas 1.422 m².
b. Sinking fund terdiri dari tiga (3) bulan pokok dan bunga sebesar Rp4,1 miliar.

Pada tanggal 12 Maret 2020, BA telah menerima surat pemberitahuan Pengalihan Piutang dari TPI kepada Koperasi Simpan Pinjam Timur Pratama Indonesia ("Kospin TPI") berdasarkan Perjanjian Jual Beli Piutang antara TPI dan Kospin TPI pada tanggal 26 Februari 2020. Efektif sejak tanggal surat pemberitahuan, pinjaman BA dari TPI telah beralih ke Kospin TPI.

Pada tanggal 13 Juli 2021, BA dan Kospin TPI telah menandatangani Perjanjian Penyelesaian Pinjaman, yang menegaskan bahwa pinjaman BA kepada Kospin TPI sebesar Rp29,40 miliar, yang terdiri dari utang pokok sebesar Rp18,13 miliar dan bunga sebesar Rp11,27 miliar. Jangka waktu perjanjian ini berlaku selama enam puluh (60) bulan.

Berdasarkan Perjanjian Pinjaman, BA dianggap telah wanprestasi jika tidak melakukan pembayaran atas angsuran selama dua (2) bulan berturut-turut dan Kospin TPI berhak untuk memulai pelaksanaan lelang terbuka atas jaminan pinjaman. Atas setiap keterlambatan pembayaran angsuran, BA akan dikenakan denda sebesar 10% dari besarnya angsuran setiap bulan.

Pada bulan Desember 2024, BA telah menyelesaikan seluruh kewajiban atas fasilitas pinjaman ini.

Pada tanggal 31 Desember 2024 dan 2023, saldo pinjaman utang kepada Kospin TPI masing-masing sebesar nihil dan Rp15,70 miliar.

## 22. LONG-TERM LOANS (Continued)

On November 6, 2017, BA entered into a Mutual Agreement with PT Timur Properti Investindo TPI to obtain loan with maximum credit limit of Rp25.00 billion. Based on TPI's Approval Letter regarding BA's Debt Settlement Plan on February 11, 2020, the maturity date of this loan has been extended until June 2026.

The loan is secured by:

a. One (1) unit of office space located at Bakrie Tower, 35th Floor with land area of 1,422 m².
b. Sinking fund comprised of three (3) months of principal and interest totalling Rp4.1 billion.

On March 12, 2020, BA received notification letter of the Transfer Receivable from TPI to Koperasi Simpan Pinjam Timur Pratama Indonesia ("Kospin TPI") based on Sale and Purchase of Receivable Agreement between TPI and Kospin TPI on February 26, 2020. Effective since the date of notification letter, BA loan from TPI has been transferred to Kospin TPI.

On July 13 2021, BA and Kospin TPI signed a Loan Settlement Agreement, which stated that BA's loan to Kospin TPI was Rp29.40 billion, consisting of a principal loan amounting to Rp18.13 billion and interest amounting to Rp11.27 billion. The term of this agreement is valid for sixty (60) months.

According to the Loan Agreement, BA is considered to be in default if it fails to make payments for two (2) consecutive months, and Kospin TPI has the right to initiate an open auction for the collateral of the loan. For each installment payment delay, BA will be charged a penalty of 10% of the installment amount per month.

In December 2024, BA has fully settled all the obligation related to this loan facility.

# Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)

As part of efforts to improve sustainable corporate governance, BTN has completed a Diagnostic Review of its Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). This process represents a strategic initiative aligned with the directives of the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (KBUMN) based on KBUMN Letter No. S-4/DKU.MBU/02/2024. As part of efforts to strengthen corporate governance, BTN's ICOFR Diagnostic Review project is implemented through a systematic approach consisting of four main stages:

## Stages of Diagnostic Review for ICOFR at BTN

1.  Mapping BTN's corporate structure and assessing risks of material misstatements due to structural complexity. The results serve as a basis for understanding potential risks in financial reporting.

2.  Identifying significant accounts in BTN's financial statements. Each account is analyzed to assess the risks attached, ensuring all elements affecting internal controls are appropriately mapped.

3.  Conducting diagnostic procedures to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in various areas. This process includes interviews with process owners, document reviews of policies and procedures, and in-depth analysis of control implementation.

4.  Comprehensive improvement recommendations are drafted. An implementation roadmap is also designed as a strategic guide for executing improvements in a phased and measurable manner.

Throughout the process, the diagnostic procedures include in-depth interviews, regulatory documents and supporting materials reviews, and identifying areas of control that require improvement. This approach ensures that each step contributes significantly to strengthening BTN's internal controls to support transparent and accountable corporate governance.

In conducting the Diagnostic Review of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR), BTN identified 13 key areas as primary focuses, covering Entity Level Control, IT General Control, and processes in financial, credit, treasury, and HR functions. This process is designed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls across various operational lines of the Bank.

## Diagnostic Review Procedure for ICOFR at BTN

- Understanding processes and controls through interviews with Process Owners and reviews of policy and procedure documents.
- Workthrough
- Controls identified are confirmed through supporting documents for implementation.
- Confirmation
- Reviewing samples of transaction documents to assess the adequacy of controls within a transaction cycle.
- Document Review
- Identifying control areas that require improvement and obtaining confirmation from Process Owners for approval.
- Identification of Areas for Improvement

Based on the diagnostic results, BTN then prepares a roadmap to ensure the timely and efficient implementation of recommendations. The roadmap preparation involves intensive discussions with BTN management to align all improvement steps with the Company's operational needs. The primary focuses of the roadmap include:

1. Setting implementation priorities based on the risk level and urgency of each recommendation.
2. Continuous monitoring and evaluation to ensure the implementation proceeds as planned and has a positive impact on internal control management.

Additionally, through the implementation of the ICOFR Diagnostic Review, BTN reaffirms its commitment to the principles of Good Corporate Governance. This effort is designed to strengthen internal controls while enhancing transparency and accountability in financial reporting. These steps not only support efficient operational management but also serve as an essential foundation for ensuring BTN's business sustainability in facing future challenges in the banking industry.

# Basel Implementation

Basel is an international regulatory framework designed to strengthen the stability of the banking system by improving risk management. In the Indonesian banking sector, Basel implementation is carried out in accordance with OJK regulations to ensure adequate capital, liquidity, and risk management operations.

This framework supports the sustainability of banking businesses by maintaining customer trust and the stability of the financial sector. To implement risk management, particularly the application of Basel II and Basel III, which applies to all commercial banks, BTN has fulfilled the following requirements:

|  Requirement | Status  |
| --- | --- |
|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 1  |   |
|  The Bank has implemented market risk measurements using the standardized model in accordance with SE OJK No. 38/SEOJK.03/2016, dated September 15, 2016, concerning the Guidelines for Using the Standard Method in Calculating Minimum Capital Requirements for Commercial Banks by Considering Market Risk. The portfolio included in determining the KPMM market risk consists of interest rate trading book portfolios and currency trading book and banking book portfolios for exchange rate risk. The Bank has prepared SEOJK No. 23/SEOJK.03/2022, dated December 7, 2022, regarding the Calculation of Risk-Weighted Assets for Market Risk for Commercial Banks, which has been applied as of January 1, 2024. The Bank has also conducted trial calculations and reporting to OJK for market risk ATMR positions as of June 2023, September 2023, and December 2023. | ☑  |
|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 2  |   |
|  The Bank submitted the results of the implementation report on Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB) and the IRRBB calculation report to regulators quarterly in accordance with SE OJK No. 12/SEOJK.03/2018, dated August 21, 2018, concerning the Implementation of Risk Management and Measurement of Risk Using the Standard Method for Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB). | ☑  |
|  Implementation of Basel III  |   |
|  In accordance with the regulatory plan to implement Basel III as stipulated in OJK Regulation No. 11/POJK.03/2016, the Bank specifically has maintained a Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) of 20.17%, exceeding the minimum requirement of the Basel III framework, which is 10.5%. | ☑  |

# Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)

As part of efforts to improve sustainable corporate governance, BTN has completed a Diagnostic Review of its Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). This process represents a strategic initiative aligned with the directives of the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (KBUMN) based on KBUMN Letter No. S-4/DKU.MBU/02/2024. As part of efforts to strengthen corporate governance, BTN's ICOFR Diagnostic Review project is implemented through a systematic approach consisting of four main stages:

## Stages of Diagnostic Review for ICOFR at BTN

1.  Mapping BTN's corporate structure and assessing risks of material misstatements due to structural complexity. The results serve as a basis for understanding potential risks in financial reporting.

2.  Identifying significant accounts in BTN's financial statements. Each account is analyzed to assess the risks attached, ensuring all elements affecting internal controls are appropriately mapped.

3.  Conducting diagnostic procedures to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in various areas. This process includes interviews with process owners, document reviews of policies and procedures, and in-depth analysis of control implementation.

4.  Comprehensive improvement recommendations are drafted. An implementation roadmap is also designed as a strategic guide for executing improvements in a phased and measurable manner.

Throughout the process, the diagnostic procedures include in-depth interviews, regulatory documents and supporting materials reviews, and identifying areas of control that require improvement. This approach ensures that each step contributes significantly to strengthening BTN's internal controls to support transparent and accountable corporate governance.

In conducting the Diagnostic Review of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR), BTN identified 13 key areas as primary focuses, covering Entity Level Control, IT General Control, and processes in financial, credit, treasury, and HR functions. This process is designed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls across various operational lines of the Bank.

## Diagnostic Review Procedure for ICOFR at BTN

- Understanding processes and controls through interviews with Process Owners and reviews of policy and procedure documents.
- Workthrough
- Controls identified are confirmed through supporting documents for implementation.
- Confirmation
- Reviewing samples of transaction documents to assess the adequacy of controls within a transaction cycle.
- Document Review
- Identifying control areas that require improvement and obtaining confirmation from Process Owners for approval.
- Identification of Areas for Improvement

# Basel Implementation

Basel is an international regulatory framework designed to strengthen the stability of the banking system by improving risk management. In the Indonesian banking sector, Basel implementation is carried out in accordance with OJK regulations to ensure adequate capital, liquidity, and risk management operations.

This framework supports the sustainability of banking businesses by maintaining customer trust and the stability of the financial sector. To implement risk management, particularly the application of Basel II and Basel III, which applies to all commercial banks, BTN has fulfilled the following requirements:

|  The Bank has implemented market risk measurements using the standardized model in accordance with SE OJK No. 38/SEOJK.03/2016, dated September 15, 2016, concerning the Guidelines for Using the Standard Method in Calculating Minimum Capital Requirements for Commercial Banks by Considering Market Risk. The portfolio included in determining the KPMM market risk consists of interest rate trading book portfolios and currency trading book and banking book portfolios for exchange rate risk. # Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)

As part of efforts to improve sustainable corporate governance, BTN has completed a Diagnostic Review of its Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). This process represents a strategic initiative aligned with the directives of the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (KBUMN) based on KBUMN Letter No. S-4/DKU.MBU/02/2024. As part of efforts to strengthen corporate governance, BTN's ICOFR Diagnostic Review project is implemented through a systematic approach consisting of four main stages:

## Stages of Diagnostic Review for ICOFR at BTN

1.  Mapping BTN's corporate structure and assessing risks of material misstatements due to structural complexity. The results serve as a basis for understanding potential risks in financial reporting.

2.  Identifying significant accounts in BTN's financial statements. Each account is analyzed to assess the risks attached, ensuring all elements affecting internal controls are appropriately mapped.

3.  Conducting diagnostic procedures to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in various areas. This process includes interviews with process owners, document reviews of policies and procedures, and in-depth analysis of control implementation.

4.  Comprehensive improvement recommendations are drafted. An implementation roadmap is also designed as a strategic guide for executing improvements in a phased and measurable manner.

Throughout the process, the diagnostic procedures include in-depth interviews, regulatory documents and supporting materials reviews, and identifying areas of control that require improvement. This approach ensures that each step contributes significantly to strengthening BTN's internal controls to support transparent and accountable corporate governance.

In conducting the Diagnostic Review of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR), BTN identified 13 key areas as primary focuses, covering Entity Level Control, IT General Control, and processes in financial, credit, treasury, and HR functions. This process is designed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls across various operational lines of the Bank.

## Diagnostic Review Procedure for ICOFR at BTN

- Understanding processes and controls through interviews with Process Owners and reviews of policy and procedure documents.
- Workthrough
- Controls identified are confirmed through supporting documents for implementation.
- Confirmation
- Reviewing samples of transaction documents to assess the adequacy of controls within a transaction cycle.
- Document Review
- Identifying control areas that require improvement and obtaining confirmation from Process Owners for approval.
- Identification of Areas for Improvement

# Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)

As part of efforts to improve sustainable corporate governance, BTN has completed a Diagnostic Review of its Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). This process represents a strategic initiative aligned with the directives of the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (KBUMN) based on KBUMN Letter No. S-4/DKU.MBU/02/2024. As part of efforts to strengthen corporate governance, BTN's ICOFR Diagnostic Review project is implemented through a systematic approach consisting of four main stages:

## Stages of Diagnostic Review for ICOFR at BTN

1.  Mapping BTN's corporate structure and assessing risks of material misstatements due to structural complexity. The results serve as a basis for understanding potential risks in financial reporting.

2.  Identifying significant accounts in BTN's financial statements. Each account is analyzed to assess the risks attached, ensuring all elements affecting internal controls are appropriately mapped.

3.  Conducting diagnostic procedures to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in various areas. This process includes interviews with process owners, document reviews of policies and procedures, and in-depth analysis of control implementation.

4.  Comprehensive improvement recommendations are drafted. An implementation roadmap is also designed as a strategic guide for executing improvements in a phased and measurable manner.

Throughout the process, the diagnostic procedures include in-depth interviews, regulatory documents and supporting materials reviews, and identifying areas of control that require improvement. This approach ensures that each step contributes significantly to strengthening BTN's internal controls to support transparent and accountable corporate governance.

In conducting the Diagnostic Review of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR), BTN identified 13 key areas as primary focuses, covering Entity Level Control, IT General Control, and processes in financial, credit, treasury, and HR functions. This process is designed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls across various operational lines of the Bank.

## Diagnostic Review Procedure for ICOFR at BTN

- Understanding processes and controls through interviews with Process Owners and reviews of policy and procedure documents.
- Workthrough
- Controls identified are confirmed through supporting documents for implementation.
- Confirmation
- Reviewing samples of transaction documents to assess the adequacy of controls within a transaction cycle.
- Document Review
- Identifying control areas that require improvement and obtaining confirmation from Process Owners for approval.
- Identification of Areas for Improvement

Based on the diagnostic results, BTN then prepares a roadmap to ensure the timely and efficient implementation of recommendations. The roadmap preparation involves intensive discussions with BTN management to align all improvement steps with the Company's operational needs. The primary focuses of the roadmap include:

1. Setting implementation priorities based on the risk level and urgency of each recommendation.
2. Continuous monitoring and evaluation to ensure the implementation proceeds as planned and has a positive impact on internal control management.

Additionally, through the implementation of the ICOFR Diagnostic Review, BTN reaffirms its commitment to the principles of Good Corporate Governance. This effort is designed to strengthen internal controls while enhancing transparency and accountability in financial reporting. These steps not only support efficient operational management but also serve as an essential foundation for ensuring BTN's business sustainability in facing future challenges in the banking industry.

# Basel Implementation

Basel is an international regulatory framework designed to strengthen the stability of the banking system by improving risk management. In the Indonesian banking sector, Basel implementation is carried out in accordance with OJK regulations to ensure adequate capital, liquidity, and risk management operations.

This framework supports the sustainability of banking businesses by maintaining customer trust and the stability of the financial sector. To implement risk management, particularly the application of Basel II and Basel III, which applies to all commercial banks, BTN has fulfilled the following requirements:

|  Requirement | Status  |
| --- | --- |
|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 1  |   |
|  The Bank has implemented market risk measurements using the standardized model in accordance with SE OJK No. 38/SEOJK.03/2016, dated September 15, 2016, concerning the Guidelines for Using the Standard Method in Calculating Minimum Capital Requirements for Commercial Banks by Considering Market Risk. The portfolio included in determining the KPMM market risk consists of interest rate trading book portfolios and currency trading book and banking book portfolios for exchange rate risk. The Bank has prepared SEOJK No. 23/SEOJK.03/2022, dated December 7, 2022, regarding the Calculation of Risk-Weighted Assets for Market Risk for Commercial Banks, which has been applied as of January 1, 2024. The Bank has also conducted trial calculations and reporting to OJK for market risk ATMR positions as of June 2023, September 2023, and December 2023. | ☑  |
|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 2  |   |
|  The Bank submitted the results of the implementation report on Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB) and the IRRBB calculation report to regulators quarterly in accordance with SE OJK No. 12/SEOJK.03/2018, dated August 21, 2018, concerning the Implementation of Risk Management and Measurement of Risk Using the Standard Method for Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB). | ☑  |
|  Implementation of Basel III  |   |
|  In accordance with the regulatory plan to implement Basel III as stipulated in OJK Regulation No. 11/POJK.03/2016, the Bank specifically has maintained a Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) of 20.17%, exceeding the minimum requirement of the Basel III framework, which is 10.5%. | ☑  |

# Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)

As part of efforts to improve sustainable corporate governance, BTN has completed a Diagnostic Review of its Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). This process represents a strategic initiative aligned with the directives of the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (KBUMN) based on KBUMN Letter No. S-4/DKU.MBU/02/2024. As part of efforts to strengthen corporate governance, BTN's ICOFR Diagnostic Review project is implemented through a systematic approach consisting of four main stages:

## Stages of Diagnostic Review for ICOFR at BTN

1.  Mapping BTN's corporate structure and assessing risks of material misstatements due to structural complexity. The results serve as a basis for understanding potential risks in financial reporting.

2.  Identifying significant accounts in BTN's financial statements. Each account is analyzed to assess the risks attached, ensuring all elements affecting internal controls are appropriately mapped.

3.  Conducting diagnostic procedures to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in various areas. This process includes interviews with process owners, document reviews of policies and procedures, and in-depth analysis of control implementation.

4.  Comprehensive improvement recommendations are drafted. An implementation roadmap is also designed as a strategic guide for executing improvements in a phased and measurable manner.

Throughout the process, the diagnostic procedures include in-depth interviews, regulatory documents and supporting materials reviews, and identifying areas of control that require improvement. This approach ensures that each step contributes significantly to strengthening BTN's internal controls to support transparent and accountable corporate governance.

In conducting the Diagnostic Review of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR), BTN identified 13 key areas as primary focuses, covering Entity Level Control, IT General Control, and processes in financial, credit, treasury, and HR functions. This process is designed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls across various operational lines of the Bank.

## Diagnostic Review Procedure for ICOFR at BTN

- Understanding processes and controls through interviews with Process Owners and reviews of policy and procedure documents.
- Workthrough
- Controls identified are confirmed through supporting documents for implementation.
- Confirmation
- Reviewing samples of transaction documents to assess the adequacy of controls within a transaction cycle.
- Document Review
- Identifying control areas that require improvement and obtaining confirmation from Process Owners for approval.
- Identification of Areas for Improvement

Based on the diagnostic results, BTN then prepares a roadmap to ensure the timely and efficient implementation of recommendations. The roadmap preparation involves intensive discussions with BTN management to align all improvement steps with the Company's operational needs. The primary focuses of the roadmap include:

1. Setting implementation priorities based on the risk level and urgency of each recommendation.
2. Continuous monitoring and evaluation to ensure the implementation proceeds as planned and has a positive impact on internal control management.

Additionally, through the implementation of the ICOFR Diagnostic Review, BTN reaffirms its commitment to the principles of Good Corporate Governance. This effort is designed to strengthen internal controls while enhancing transparency and accountability in financial reporting. These steps not only support efficient operational management but also serve as an essential foundation for ensuring BTN's business sustainability in facing future challenges in the banking industry.

# Basel Implementation

Basel is an international regulatory framework designed to strengthen the stability of the banking system by improving risk management. In the Indonesian banking sector, Basel implementation is carried out in accordance with OJK regulations to ensure adequate capital, liquidity, and risk management operations.

This framework supports the sustainability of banking businesses by maintaining customer trust and the stability of the financial sector. To implement risk management, particularly the application of Basel II and Basel III, which applies to all commercial banks, BTN has fulfilled the following requirements:

|  Requirement | Status  |
| --- | --- |
|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 1  |   |
|  The Bank has implemented market risk measurements using the standardized model in accordance with SE OJK No. 38/SEOJK.03/2016, dated September 15, 2016, concerning the Guidelines for Using the Standard Method in Calculating Minimum Capital Requirements for Commercial Banks by Considering Market Risk. The portfolio included in determining the KPMM market risk consists of interest rate trading book portfolios and currency trading book and banking book portfolios for exchange rate risk. The Bank has prepared SEOJK No. 23/SEOJK.03/2022, dated December 7, 2022, regarding the Calculation of Risk-Weighted Assets for Market Risk for Commercial Banks, which has been applied as of January 1, 2024. The Bank has also conducted trial calculations and reporting to OJK for market risk ATMR positions as of June 2023, September 2023, and December 2023. | ☑  |
|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 2  |   |
|  The Bank submitted the results of the implementation report on Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB) and the IRRBB calculation report to regulators quarterly in accordance with SE OJK No. 12/SEOJK.03/2018, dated August 21, 2018, concerning the Implementation of Risk Management and Measurement of Risk Using the Standard Method for Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB). | ☑  |
|  Implementation of Basel III  |   |
|  In accordance with the regulatory plan to implement Basel III as stipulated in OJK Regulation No. 11/POJK.03/2016, the Bank specifically has maintained a Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) of 20.17%, exceeding the minimum requirement of the Basel III framework, which is 10.5%. | ☑  |

# Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)

As part of efforts to improve sustainable corporate governance, BTN has completed a Diagnostic Review of its Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). This process represents a strategic initiative aligned with the directives of the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (KBUMN) based on KBUMN Letter No. S-4/DKU.MBU/02/2024. As part of efforts to strengthen corporate governance, BTN's ICOFR Diagnostic Review project is implemented through a systematic approach consisting of four main stages:

## Stages of Diagnostic Review for ICOFR at BTN

1.  Mapping BTN's corporate structure and assessing risks of material misstatements due to structural complexity. The results serve as a basis for understanding potential risks in financial reporting.

2.  Identifying significant accounts in BTN's financial statements. Each account is analyzed to assess the risks attached, ensuring all elements affecting internal controls are appropriately mapped.

3.  Conducting diagnostic procedures to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in various areas. This process includes interviews with process owners, document reviews of policies and procedures, and in-depth analysis of control implementation.

4.  Comprehensive improvement recommendations are drafted. An implementation roadmap is also designed as a strategic guide for executing improvements in a phased and measurable manner.

Throughout the process, the diagnostic procedures include in-depth interviews, regulatory documents and supporting materials reviews, and identifying areas of control that require improvement. This approach ensures that each step contributes significantly to strengthening BTN's internal controls to support transparent and accountable corporate governance.

In conducting the Diagnostic Review of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR), BTN identified 13 key areas as primary focuses, covering Entity Level Control, IT General Control, and processes in financial, credit, treasury, and HR functions. This process is designed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls across various operational lines of the Bank.

## Diagnostic Review Procedure for ICOFR at BTN

- Understanding processes and controls through interviews with Process Owners and reviews of policy and procedure documents.
- Workthrough
- Controls identified are confirmed through supporting documents for implementation.
- Confirmation
- Reviewing samples of transaction documents to assess the adequacy of controls within a transaction cycle.
- Document Review
- Identifying control areas that require improvement and obtaining confirmation from Process Owners for approval.
- Identification of Areas for Improvement

Based on the diagnostic results, BTN then prepares a roadmap to ensure the timely and efficient implementation of recommendations. The roadmap preparation involves intensive discussions with BTN management to align all improvement steps with the Company's operational needs. The primary focuses of the roadmap include:

1. Setting implementation priorities based on the risk level and urgency of each recommendation.
2. Continuous monitoring and evaluation to ensure the implementation proceeds as planned and has a positive impact on internal control management.

Additionally, through the implementation of the ICOFR Diagnostic Review, BTN reaffirms its commitment to the principles of Good Corporate Governance. This effort is designed to strengthen internal controls while enhancing transparency and accountability in financial reporting. These steps not only support efficient operational management but also serve as an essential foundation for ensuring BTN's business sustainability in facing future challenges in the banking industry.

# Basel Implementation

Basel is an international regulatory framework designed to strengthen the stability of the banking system by improving risk management. In the Indonesian banking sector, Basel implementation is carried out in accordance with OJK regulations to ensure adequate capital, liquidity, and risk management operations.

This framework supports the sustainability of banking businesses by maintaining customer trust and the stability of the financial sector. To implement risk management, particularly the application of Basel II and Basel III, which applies to all commercial banks, BTN has fulfilled the following requirements:

|  Requirement | Status  |
| --- | --- |
|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 1  |   |
|  The Bank has implemented market risk measurements using the standardized model in accordance with SE OJK No. 38/SEOJK.03/2016, dated September 15, 2016, concerning the Guidelines for Using the Standard Method in Calculating Minimum Capital Requirements for Commercial Banks by Considering Market Risk. The portfolio included in determining the KPMM market risk consists of interest rate trading book portfolios and currency trading book and banking book portfolios for exchange rate risk. The Bank has prepared SEOJK No. 23/SEOJK.03/2022, dated December 7, 2022, regarding the Calculation of Risk-Weighted Assets for Market Risk for Commercial Banks, which has been applied as of January 1, 2024. # Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)

As part of efforts to improve sustainable corporate governance, BTN has completed a Diagnostic Review of its Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). This process represents a strategic initiative aligned with the directives of the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (KBUMN) based on KBUMN Letter No. S-4/DKU.MBU/02/2024. As part of efforts to strengthen corporate governance, BTN's ICOFR Diagnostic Review project is implemented through a systematic approach consisting of four main stages:

## Stages of Diagnostic Review for ICOFR at BTN

1.  Mapping BTN's corporate structure and assessing risks of material misstatements due to structural complexity. The results serve as a basis for understanding potential risks in financial reporting.

2.  Identifying significant accounts in BTN's financial statements. Each account is analyzed to assess the risks attached, ensuring all elements affecting internal controls are appropriately mapped.

3.  Conducting diagnostic procedures to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls in various areas. This process includes interviews with process owners, document reviews of policies and procedures, and in-depth analysis of control implementation.

4.  Comprehensive improvement recommendations are drafted. An implementation roadmap is also designed as a strategic guide for executing improvements in a phased and measurable manner.

Throughout the process, the diagnostic procedures include in-depth interviews, regulatory documents and supporting materials reviews, and identifying areas of control that require improvement. This approach ensures that each step contributes significantly to strengthening BTN's internal controls to support transparent and accountable corporate governance.

In conducting the Diagnostic Review of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICOFR), BTN identified 13 key areas as primary focuses, covering Entity Level Control, IT General Control, and processes in financial, credit, treasury, and HR functions. This process is designed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls across various operational lines of the Bank.

## Diagnostic Review Procedure for ICOFR at BTN

- Understanding processes and controls through interviews with Process Owners and reviews of policy and procedure documents.
- Workthrough
- Controls identified are confirmed through supporting documents for implementation.
- Confirmation
- Reviewing samples of transaction documents to assess the adequacy of controls within a transaction cycle.
- Document Review
- Identifying control areas that require improvement and obtaining confirmation from Process Owners for approval.
- Identification of Areas for Improvement

# Basel Implementation

Basel is an international regulatory framework designed to strengthen the stability of the banking system by improving risk management. In the Indonesian banking sector, Basel implementation is carried out in accordance with OJK regulations to ensure adequate capital, liquidity, and risk management operations.

This framework supports the sustainability of banking businesses by maintaining customer trust and the stability of the financial sector. To implement risk management, particularly the application of Basel II and Basel III, which applies to all commercial banks, BTN has fulfilled the following requirements:

|  Implementation of Basel II Pillar 1  |   |
|  The Bank has implemented market risk measurements using the standardized model in accordance with SE OJK No. 38/SEOJK.03/2016, dated September 15, 2016, concerning the Guidelines for Using the Standard Method in Calculating Minimum Capital Requirements for Commercial Banks by Considering Market Risk. The portfolio included in determining the KPMM market risk consists of interest rate trading book portfolios and currency trading book and banking book portfolios for exchange rate risk. The Bank has prepared SEOJK No. 23/SEOJK.03/2022, dated December 7, 2022, regarding the Calculation of Risk-Weighted Assets for Market Risk for Commercial Banks, which has been applied as of January 1, 2024. # Code of Conduct and Business Ethics

[GR1 2--23, 2--24]

The Code of Conduct reflects BTN's commitment to implementing Good Corporate Governance (GCG) by adhering to the highest standards based on proven best practices in the banking industry that have established credibility and trustworthiness. In the context of ethics, the credibility and trust held by the public, shareholders, and customers are considered significant factors in supporting the Bank's growth and sustainability. Therefore, every business activity carried out by BTN not only complies with applicable laws and regulations but also reflects adherence to norms and ethics prevailing in society and business environments.

Awareness of the importance of good ethical practices plays a key role in building BTN's positive reputation, ultimately strengthening its image as a socially responsible entity that contributes positively to society. To support this goal, BTN is committed to upholding integrity in every action and decision taken. The Bank does so by applying ethical guidelines and clear behavior standards as a foundation for all members of the organization in carrying out their responsibilities. These guidelines ensure that every individual and team at BTN works professionally and in accordance with high ethical standards, aligned with BTN's principles, vision, mission, and established values, while adhering to applicable internal and external regulations.

To ensure that every activity reflects a commitment to ethical principles, BTN has established standards of ethics and conduct aligned with its vision, mission, and values. These standards are implemented through Joint Decision Letter of the Board of Commissioners No. 01/SKPB/KOM/BTN/2024 and Board of Directors No. SKPB-01/DIR/BTN/2024 on BTN's Code of Conduct and Behavior (Code of Conduct). This Code provides clear guidelines for all BTN employees to act in accordance with the upheld values, maintaining integrity and professionalism in all aspects of operations. Non-compliance or deviations from the Code of Conduct can result in significant reputational damage, operational risk, reduced business efficiency and effectiveness, or credit risk, impacting the Bank's ability to manage and provide loans responsibly. Therefore, business ethics play a critical role in maintaining BTN's sustainability and stability.

The Code of Conduct aims to shape behavior that aligns with the ideal standards and fosters a work culture based on BTN's core values. The Code of Conduct consists of four main chapters, which are briefly described as follows:

### 1. Introduction

The Code of Conduct is a codification or compilation of policies, regulations, and agreements jointly made between the Bank and its employees, designed to influence and establish the expected behavior standards for all individuals in the organization, from management to employees. The main objective is to ensure that all activities carried out within the Bank adhere to high ethical standards. The application of the Code of Conduct, in terms of both compliance and breaches, becomes one of the indicators in evaluating employee performance. In other words, as long as employees adhere to the Code of Conduct, it will positively influence their performance evaluations. The Code of Conduct not only serves as a reference for decision-making and policy implementation but also acts as a foundation for managing the Bank's practices. Consistency in applying the Code of Conduct demonstrates BTN's commitment to always conducting its business with high ethical values and good principles. This, in turn, supports the establishment of Good Corporate Governance (GCG).

### 2. Business Ethics Standards

The business ethics standards function as a guide that governs the behavior and interactions of the Bank across various aspects of its activities. These ethical guidelines include relationships between the Bank and related parties, such as employees, customers, suppliers of goods and services, and competitors. In addition, these standards also encompass ethics in relations with work partners, the government, society, the media, and professional organizations. All interactions must be carried out with principles of honesty, transparency, and mutual respect, to maintain the Bank's reputation and integrity.

3. Policy on Employee Conduct Standards
- Employees must avoid conditions, situations, or impressions of a conflict of interest or abuse of authority.
- Members of the Board of Commissioners, Directors, and Bank employees are prohibited from giving or receiving anything of value, whether directly or indirectly, from business partners that could influence decision-making.
- The Bank is committed to engaging in fair and ethical business competition in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The Bank avoids monopolistic practices, provides equal opportunities to all business players, and promotes sustainable business innovation while complying with all prevailing laws and regulations.
- Bank organs and employees must adhere to laws, regulations, and Bank policies.

4. Implementation and Enforcement
All BTN employees are obligated to report any breaches or deviations from the Corporate Code of Conduct to the Human Capital Management & Culture Specialist Division. BTN guarantees that the reporter's identity will be protected with full confidentiality to avoid retaliation or negative repercussions. Upon receiving the report, the Human Capital Management Division conducts a thorough analysis and submits its evaluation

to the Board of Directors and/or Commissioners, depending on their responsibilities and authority. Based on the assessment results, the Board of Directors and Commissioners will decide the necessary actions, such as coaching, disciplinary sanctions, or corrective actions. In addition, the Bank continues to develop and establish preventive procedures and policies that all supervisors must follow within the work environment to ensure that similar breaches do not recur in the future. [GRI 2-16]

The Business Ethics and Code of Conduct document is accessible to all parties through BTN's official website to ensure transparency and accountability. This code not only outlines the expected standards of conduct within a business context but also emphasizes respect for human rights, in line with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGP BHR). It affirms the Bank's commitment to operating responsibly and upholding the rights of individuals in all business activities. Furthermore, all decisions and actions taken by the Bank adhere to the principles of prudence, meaning that every decision and activity is conducted with careful consideration and accountability. BTN's Code of Ethics also requires all parties involved to perform due diligence, including customer verification, business partner inspections, and assessments of other related parties, to ensure compliance with ethical standards and laws established by BTN. [GRI 2-23]

Compliance with the Code of Conduct

The Code of Conduct applies to all members of the highest governance bodies and employees in every business activity of the Bank, including interactions with stakeholders. The implementation of this code is regulated under the Joint Decision Letter of the Board of Commissioners No. 01/SKPB/KOM/BTN/2024 and Board of Directors No. SKPB-01/DIR/BTN/2024 concerning the Code of Conduct of PT Bank Tabungan Negara (Persero) Tbk. The Bank requires every individual in the organization to sign an Integrity Pact, aimed at ensuring the Code of Conduct is executed with full

accountability. The successful implementation of the Code of Conduct is the responsibility of the leaders in each work unit, who must ensure that all employees understand and properly adhere to the code within their work environment.

BTN implements the Code of Conduct comprehensively, covering education, campaigns, application, reporting, and follow-up actions for Code of Conduct breaches. [GRI 2-23]

# Code of Conduct and Business Ethics

[GR1 2--23, 2--24]

The Code of Conduct reflects BTN's commitment to implementing Good Corporate Governance (GCG) by adhering to the highest standards based on proven best practices in the banking industry that have established credibility and trustworthiness. In the context of ethics, the credibility and trust held by the public, shareholders, and customers are considered significant factors in supporting the Bank's growth and sustainability. Therefore, every business activity carried out by BTN not only complies with applicable laws and regulations but also reflects adherence to norms and ethics prevailing in society and business environments.

Awareness of the importance of good ethical practices plays a key role in building BTN's positive reputation, ultimately strengthening its image as a socially responsible entity that contributes positively to society. To support this goal, BTN is committed to upholding integrity in every action and decision taken. The Bank does so by applying ethical guidelines and clear behavior standards as a foundation for all members of the organization in carrying out their responsibilities. These guidelines ensure that every individual and team at BTN works professionally and in accordance with high ethical standards, aligned with BTN's principles, vision, mission, and established values, while adhering to applicable internal and external regulations.

To ensure that every activity reflects a commitment to ethical principles, BTN has established standards of ethics and conduct aligned with its vision, mission, and values. These standards are implemented through Joint Decision Letter of the Board of Commissioners No. 01/SKPB/KOM/BTN/2024 and Board of Directors No. SKPB-01/DIR/BTN/2024 on BTN's Code of Conduct and Behavior (Code of Conduct). This Code provides clear guidelines for all BTN employees to act in accordance with the upheld values, maintaining integrity and professionalism in all aspects of operations. Non-compliance or deviations from the Code of Conduct can result in significant reputational damage, operational risk, reduced business efficiency and effectiveness, or credit risk, impacting the Bank's ability to manage and provide loans responsibly. Therefore, business ethics play a critical role in maintaining BTN's sustainability and stability.

The Code of Conduct aims to shape behavior that aligns with the ideal standards and fosters a work culture based on BTN's core values. The Code of Conduct consists of four main chapters, which are briefly described as follows:

### 1. Introduction

The Code of Conduct is a codification or compilation of policies, regulations, and agreements jointly made between the Bank and its employees, designed to influence and establish the expected behavior standards for all individuals in the organization, from management to employees. The main objective is to ensure that all activities carried out within the Bank adhere to high ethical standards. The application of the Code of Conduct, in terms of both compliance and breaches, becomes one of the indicators in evaluating employee performance. In other words, as long as employees adhere to the Code of Conduct, it will positively influence their performance evaluations. The Code of Conduct not only serves as a reference for decision-making and policy implementation but also acts as a foundation for managing the Bank's practices. Consistency in applying the Code of Conduct demonstrates BTN's commitment to always conducting its business with high ethical values and good principles. This, in turn, supports the establishment of Good Corporate Governance (GCG).

### 2. Business Ethics Standards

The business ethics standards function as a guide that governs the behavior and interactions of the Bank across various aspects of its activities. These ethical guidelines include relationships between the Bank and related parties, such as employees, customers, suppliers of goods and services, and competitors. In addition, these standards also encompass ethics in relations with work partners, the government, society, the media, and professional organizations. All interactions must be carried out with principles of honesty, transparency, and mutual respect, to maintain the Bank's reputation and integrity.

3. Policy on Employee Conduct Standards
- Employees must avoid conditions, situations, or impressions of a conflict of interest or abuse of authority.
- Members of the Board of Commissioners, Directors, and Bank employees are prohibited from giving or receiving anything of value, whether directly or indirectly, from business partners that could influence decision-making.
- The Bank is committed to engaging in fair and ethical business competition in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The Bank avoids monopolistic practices, provides equal opportunities to all business players, and promotes sustainable business innovation while complying with all prevailing laws and regulations.
- Bank organs and employees must adhere to laws, regulations, and Bank policies.

4. Implementation and Enforcement
All BTN employees are obligated to report any breaches or deviations from the Corporate Code of Conduct to the Human Capital Management & Culture Specialist Division. BTN guarantees that the reporter's identity will be protected with full confidentiality to avoid retaliation or negative repercussions. Upon receiving the report, the Human Capital Management Division conducts a thorough analysis and submits its evaluation

to the Board of Directors and/or Commissioners, depending on their responsibilities and authority. Based on the assessment results, the Board of Directors and Commissioners will decide the necessary actions, such as coaching, disciplinary sanctions, or corrective actions. In addition, the Bank continues to develop and establish preventive procedures and policies that all supervisors must follow within the work environment to ensure that similar breaches do not recur in the future. [GRI 2-16]

The Business Ethics and Code of Conduct document is accessible to all parties through BTN's official website to ensure transparency and accountability. This code not only outlines the expected standards of conduct within a business context but also emphasizes respect for human rights, in line with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGP BHR). It affirms the Bank's commitment to operating responsibly and upholding the rights of individuals in all business activities. Furthermore, all decisions and actions taken by the Bank adhere to the principles of prudence, meaning that every decision and activity is conducted with careful consideration and accountability. BTN's Code of Ethics also requires all parties involved to perform due diligence, including customer verification, business partner inspections, and assessments of other related parties, to ensure compliance with ethical standards and laws established by BTN. [GRI 2-23]

Compliance with the Code of Conduct

The Code of Conduct applies to all members of the highest governance bodies and employees in every business activity of the Bank, including interactions with stakeholders. The implementation of this code is regulated under the Joint Decision Letter of the Board of Commissioners No. 01/SKPB/KOM/BTN/2024 and Board of Directors No. SKPB-01/DIR/BTN/2024 concerning the Code of Conduct of PT Bank Tabungan Negara (Persero) Tbk. The Bank requires every individual in the organization to sign an Integrity Pact, aimed at ensuring the Code of Conduct is executed with full

accountability. The successful implementation of the Code of Conduct is the responsibility of the leaders in each work unit, who must ensure that all employees understand and properly adhere to the code within their work environment.

BTN implements the Code of Conduct comprehensively, covering education, campaigns, application, reporting, and follow-up actions for Code of Conduct breaches. [GRI 2-23]

# Code of Conduct and Business Ethics

[GR1 2--23, 2--24]

The Code of Conduct reflects BTN's commitment to implementing Good Corporate Governance (GCG) by adhering to the highest standards based on proven best practices in the banking industry that have established credibility and trustworthiness. In the context of ethics, the credibility and trust held by the public, shareholders, and customers are considered significant factors in supporting the Bank's growth and sustainability. Therefore, every business activity carried out by BTN not only complies with applicable laws and regulations but also reflects adherence to norms and ethics prevailing in society and business environments.

Awareness of the importance of good ethical practices plays a key role in building BTN's positive reputation, ultimately strengthening its image as a socially responsible entity that contributes positively to society. To support this goal, BTN is committed to upholding integrity in every action and decision taken. The Bank does so by applying ethical guidelines and clear behavior standards as a foundation for all members of the organization in carrying out their responsibilities. These guidelines ensure that every individual and team at BTN works professionally and in accordance with high ethical standards, aligned with BTN's principles, vision, mission, and established values, while adhering to applicable internal and external regulations.

To ensure that every activity reflects a commitment to ethical principles, BTN has established standards of ethics and conduct aligned with its vision, mission, and values. These standards are implemented through Joint Decision Letter of the Board of Commissioners No. 01/SKPB/KOM/BTN/2024 and Board of Directors No. SKPB-01/DIR/BTN/2024 on BTN's Code of Conduct and Behavior (Code of Conduct). This Code provides clear guidelines for all BTN employees to act in accordance with the upheld values, maintaining integrity and professionalism in all aspects of operations. Non-compliance or deviations from the Code of Conduct can result in significant reputational damage, operational risk, reduced business efficiency and effectiveness, or credit risk, impacting the Bank's ability to manage and provide loans responsibly. Therefore, business ethics play a critical role in maintaining BTN's sustainability and stability.

The Code of Conduct aims to shape behavior that aligns with the ideal standards and fosters a work culture based on BTN's core values. The Code of Conduct consists of four main chapters, which are briefly described as follows:

### 1. Introduction

The Code of Conduct is a codification or compilation of policies, regulations, and agreements jointly made between the Bank and its employees, designed to influence and establish the expected behavior standards for all individuals in the organization, from management to employees. The main objective is to ensure that all activities carried out within the Bank adhere to high ethical standards. The application of the Code of Conduct, in terms of both compliance and breaches, becomes one of the indicators in evaluating employee performance. In other words, as long as employees adhere to the Code of Conduct, it will positively influence their performance evaluations. The Code of Conduct not only serves as a reference for decision-making and policy implementation but also acts as a foundation for managing the Bank's practices. Consistency in applying the Code of Conduct demonstrates BTN's commitment to always conducting its business with high ethical values and good principles. This, in turn, supports the establishment of Good Corporate Governance (GCG).

### 2. Business Ethics Standards

The business ethics standards function as a guide that governs the behavior and interactions of the Bank across various aspects of its activities. These ethical guidelines include relationships between the Bank and related parties, such as employees, customers, suppliers of goods and services, and competitors. In addition, these standards also encompass ethics in relations with work partners, the government, society, the media, and professional organizations. All interactions must be carried out with principles of honesty, transparency, and mutual respect, to maintain the Bank's reputation and integrity.

3. Policy on Employee Conduct Standards
- Employees must avoid conditions, situations, or impressions of a conflict of interest or abuse of authority.
- Members of the Board of Commissioners, Directors, and Bank employees are prohibited from giving or receiving anything of value, whether directly or indirectly, from business partners that could influence decision-making.
- The Bank is committed to engaging in fair and ethical business competition in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The Bank avoids monopolistic practices, provides equal opportunities to all business players, and promotes sustainable business innovation while complying with all prevailing laws and regulations.
- Bank organs and employees must adhere to laws, regulations, and Bank policies.

4. Implementation and Enforcement
All BTN employees are obligated to report any breaches or deviations from the Corporate Code of Conduct to the Human Capital Management & Culture Specialist Division. BTN guarantees that the reporter's identity will be protected with full confidentiality to avoid retaliation or negative repercussions. Upon receiving the report, the Human Capital Management Division conducts a thorough analysis and submits its evaluation

to the Board of Directors and/or Commissioners, depending on their responsibilities and authority. Based on the assessment results, the Board of Directors and Commissioners will decide the necessary actions, such as coaching, disciplinary sanctions, or corrective actions. In addition, the Bank continues to develop and establish preventive procedures and policies that all supervisors must follow within the work environment to ensure that similar breaches do not recur in the future. [GRI 2-16]

The Business Ethics and Code of Conduct document is accessible to all parties through BTN's official website to ensure transparency and accountability. This code not only outlines the expected standards of conduct within a business context but also emphasizes respect for human rights, in line with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGP BHR). It affirms the Bank's commitment to operating responsibly and upholding the rights of individuals in all business activities. Furthermore, all decisions and actions taken by the Bank adhere to the principles of prudence, meaning that every decision and activity is conducted with careful consideration and accountability. BTN's Code of Ethics also requires all parties involved to perform due diligence, including customer verification, business partner inspections, and assessments of other related parties, to ensure compliance with ethical standards and laws established by BTN. [GRI 2-23]

Compliance with the Code of Conduct

The Code of Conduct applies to all members of the highest governance bodies and employees in every business activity of the Bank, including interactions with stakeholders. The implementation of this code is regulated under the Joint Decision Letter of the Board of Commissioners No. 01/SKPB/KOM/BTN/2024 and Board of Directors No. SKPB-01/DIR/BTN/2024 concerning the Code of Conduct of PT Bank Tabungan Negara (Persero) Tbk. The Bank requires every individual in the organization to sign an Integrity Pact, aimed at ensuring the Code of Conduct is executed with full
